title: Infusion Pump Improvement Initiative: design across the product lifecycle
focus: A device is used, maintained, and understood within a care system; design review must span that lifecycle.

sources.title: FDA Infusion Pump Improvement Initiative
sources.locator: Initiative overview and three program goals
sources.limitations: The page summarizes a historical program and links later guidance. It is not evidence that a particular pump was cleared, clinically effective, or corrected successfully.

facts.statement: The FDA describes pump problems that can cause over-infusion, under-infusion, or missed treatment.
The 2010 initiative combined stronger expectations for manufacturers, proactive design improvement, and increased user awareness across the lifecycle.

retrospective.boundary: Pump, drug library, programming, patient connection, clinicians, training, maintenance, incident reporting, and manufacturer response form the delivery system.
interfaces: Design → clinical use: interface behavior and alarms interact with workflow and interruptions.
Service history → design revision: field signals need configuration, reproducibility, and consequence context.

decision.question: What should a design-improvement program evaluate beyond component reliability?
options: Concentrate exclusively on pump mechanism accuracy.
Evaluate programming, delivery, alarms, maintenance, and field feedback as connected activities.
decision.recommendation: Trace each hazard to the lifecycle stages where it can be introduced, detected, or controlled.
decision.uncertainty: Program existence does not establish measured clinical benefit or the safety of an individual product.

rows: Connect intended therapy entry to device configuration
Specify detectable conditions and user response
Retain configuration, context, and action history
Incident review with verified corrective closure

questions: Why can technically accurate pumping still fail the clinical task?
Which information makes a field incident useful for design learning?
Explain what can and cannot be concluded from a regulator launching an improvement program.
answer_signals: Includes workflow, maintenance, and feedback beyond hardware.
Keeps historical program goals separate from proven outcomes.
Defines evidence for a product-specific claim.
retrospective.transfer_exercise: Synthetic: create an evidence plan for an alert redesign using a nonclinical bench setting and representative users. Keep clinical efficacy as a separate question.
retrospective.limits: No claim about present legal requirements, device approval, treatment settings, or patient outcomes is made.
